documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary — Acute Bronchitis
documents.rawTextExcerpt:
ALLERGIES: Severe Penicillin Allergy. Patient reported childhood rash, widespread hives & mild throat tightness after oral amoxicillin.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS: Metformin 500mg PO daily with evening meal. Albuterol MDI PRN.

documents.title: Formal IgE Penicillin Skin Prick & Graded Oral Challenge
documents.rawTextExcerpt: PROCEDURE: Skin prick with penicilloyl-polylysine (Pre-Pen) and minor determinant mixture: NEGATIVE at 20 min. Graded oral challenge with Amoxicillin 250mg completed with 60 minute observation: Zero erythema, pruritus, or respiratory distress. CONCLUSION: Patient is NOT penicillin allergic; allergy de-label recommended.

ADMISSION DIAGNOSIS: Acute viral gastroenteritis with dehydration.
ALLERGIES: Penicillin allergy — rash and hives reported following childhood amoxicillin.

CHIEF COMPLAINT: Penicillin allergy de-labeling assessment.
FINDINGS: Full skin prick test negative. Oral amoxicillin 250mg challenge tolerated without reaction.
